messages.subject: Memory Usage Spike
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

Firstly, thanks for the amazing software, which is heavily used by the HIV Inference Group at Imperial College London.

We have developed a Bayesian spatio-temporal model for circumcision in TMB. An example of it's use can be found here <https://github.com/mrc-ide/threemc_example>. I won't go into too much detail on this model here, as I feel this repo provides a reasonable reproducible example.

One issue that we have found is that during the "optimising tape ..." stage of running our optimiser, we experience a substantial memory usage spike (< 500GB for large models) (again, this is better elaborated on in our example repo). This spike appears to be associated with the TMB code from this line down <https://github.com/mrc-ide/threemc_example/blob/a67d2491119eb1904846707f2074817767872d9b/src/threemc.cpp#L209>, which involves calculations using several high-dimensional sparse matrices representing our random effects. The (temporarily) large memory usage of this model means it is very demanding on our
high-performance cluster.

We’re trying to understand:
- Why does the memory spike like this?
- Can we predict the size of the memory spike from size in input data, number of parameters etc.
- Can we save out the optimised tape and then use this for multiple model fits? This could allow us to do the costly optimisation on a beefy node but then run the rest of the simulation on smaller nodes.

Any help would be greatly appreciated.

Many Thanks,
Paddy O'Toole,
Research Assistant,
Imperial College London

messages.subject: Re: Memory Usage Spike
messages.body_plain:
You may be able to get rid of the memory spike simply by switching AD library - see ?TMB::compile.
I suggest you try:

- Add framework='TMBad' to compilation.
- Remove flags '-O0 -g' (slows down the model)

Then recompile the package.

messages.subject: tmbstan not working at all for me?
messages.subject_clean: tmbstan not working at all for me?
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

My apologies in advance if this question doesn't have sufficient information to be answer-able; I'll happily provide anything else I can if that's the case. In short, I can't get the tmbstan package to work at all. I have a TMB function (let's call it "func" here) that, although being quite complex and somewhat slow, works and gives me good MLE's for the data I provide it. No errors or issues. But when I run

tmbstan(func)

I get a "Fatal R Error" and am forced to restart RStudio entirely. I found this a bit odd so I wanted to make sure the simple example provided by the tmbstan package would work. Turns out, that didn't evaluate either - same fatal error. I've attached a screenshot of my console output taken seconds before the fatal error (it's named Picture1.png; sorry if the quality is not fantastic but hopefully it's readable).

I'm running R 4.2.3 on Windows using the RStudio IDE (version 2023.03). As far as I know these are the most up-to-date versions of R and RStudio. I tried re-installing the TMB, rstan, and tmbstan packages - but still no luck. I'm guessing this is probably something happening in my local directory / namespace (maybe there's some function that's being over-written by another package? maybe a C++ library of some sort that I'm missing somehow?) so I've posted it here rather than as a Github issue, but if others find the same issue on their devices, maybe it's not just me.

Any kind of help is greatly appreciated. Thanks!
Peter R. Thompson

messages.subject_clean: [TMB users] tmbstan not working at all for me?
messages.body_plain:
Hi.
One of the most likely possibilities might lie in an index problem.  The set of "TMB - R -  R studio" in the Windows machine is too sensitive to an error in indexing, I observe.   What I mean with an "indexing" error is a mismatch between your intending to point an element in an array and the corresponding element.   Whenever running into the mismatch problem, the R studio is forced to terminate.  This is very annoying, and thus a few friends, who use TMB, recommend we should use Linux or Mac for TMB instead of Windows.  Anyhow returning back to my main point, please check whether, in your loop (e.g., for, while, etc.) in your CPP file, your indices were correct.  Recall that the TMB index starts at zero (i.e., i =0, not i=1).   Your attachment does not show your CPP file, and thus I am not sure though that my guess is right.
Saang-Yoon

messages.body_plain:
Could be a few things. func is what is normally called 'obj' right? You don't for instance pass func=obj$fn to tmbstan -- it needs the whole object.

Does the code at https://github.com/kaskr/tmbstan#examples run? If yes, then it seems related to your specific model. I'd try tmbstan(func, chains=1, iter=200, init='last.best.par', control=list(max_treedepth=2)) and see if that runs. Also try it outside of Rstudio.

-Cole

messages.subject: Re: Memory Usage Spike
messages.body_plain:
Yes, TMBad framework can perform sparse hessian compression. However, this *not* needed/recommended except for very special model structures (has to be enabled using 'TMB::config()'). In fact the sparse hessian compression might make things worse!
Memory reductions and speedups can be expected by simply switching the framework - nothing else.

You are right that the documentation doesn't yet contain the appropriate information.
